summary: Γ is discrete because only finitely many points of 𝖴_c(g) lie over a compact set; a countable discrete group with counting measure has a cutoff.

steps.claim: Γ is discrete: the inclusion of Γ into ∏_v G₁ (a continuous map) tends to infinity along the cofinite filter, because every compact set contains the images of only finitely many elements (finite_classUnip_inter_compact with f = id, the map u ↦ its matrices being injective).

    (tendsto_cofinite_cocompact_iff.2 fun _ ↦ .of_injOn (fun ⟨_, u, _, rfl⟩ ↦ (⟨·, u, rfl⟩))
    Units.val_injective.injOn.injective.comp_left.injOn.injective.injOn ∘
    S.finite_classUnip_inter_compact c id)

steps.claim: Take the cutoff β of the counting measure on Γ (hasCutoff_count); it is measurable, and for every y the sum over u ∈ K of β(ratToInf(u)·y) equals the counting-measure integral over Γ, because K → Γ is a bijection (ratToInf is injective on matrices); this integral is 1. With step 1 this gives the four claims.
